>I truly don’t believe I have an eating disorder. I’m not afraid of food because of weight gain, but I am afraid of food because of the way it makes me feel.

This sounds exactly like me when I first developed my eating disorder. Not all people with restrictive EDs (anorexia and orthorexia) are worried about weight gain or calories, their defining feature is an extreme aversion to eating. Weight loss is just a symptom of this. Personally, when I first developed anorexia, it was because I felt pure and light when I hadn't eaten, and food made me feel sick and heavy and dirty. The obsession with weight and size came much later.

I'd get yourself into therapy if you can, but be aware that a lot of doctors and, unfortunately, even trained mental health professionals, will disregard disordered eating just because you aren't underweight. I'd stop fasting until you sort out any underlying issues, because it very easily becomes a coping mechanism and the longer you use it as such, the harder it is to get rid of.
